clue.text: Payment from the foreign king invested in state

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, so the next pieces go into the word for state

parts.note: to state is to say
la is 'the' in French, a foreign tongue
R is the abbreviation for king (Latin rex)

explanation.surface: Money sent from an overseas monarch has been put into a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the foreign' asks for a foreign language's word for 'the', here French; 'state' is the verb, not a country.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular wage paid to an employee is a form of payment.

clue.text: Essayist said to plagiarise

indicators.note: said tells us the word is heard rather than read, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to plagiarise is to steal another's work

explanation.surface: A writer is accused of copying others' work.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Steele was an 18th-century essayist who co-founded The Spectator.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Steele is a famous early English essayist, so he is an example of a writer of essays.

clue.text: Fire shot over head, getting Liverpudlian in a stew

parts.note: to lob is to send a shot high over an opponent's head
a Scouse is a native of Liverpool

explanation.surface: A gunshot over someone's head lands a man from Liverpool in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a stew' looks like the surface's 'in trouble', but 'a stew' is the definition: lobscouse is the sailors' stew that gave Liverpudlians the nickname Scouse.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a meat and vegetable hotpot once eaten by sailors, a kind of stew.

clue.text: Tree that's pale gold up on top

indicators.note: on top places the gold piece above the pale piece in the down entry
in a down clue up means the word for gold is read from bottom to top

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
wan means pale

explanation.surface: A tree with pale leaves and a golden crown.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold as OR is the heraldic term; in a down entry 'up' reads it bottom to top and 'on top' sets it above the pale word.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain ash, with its red berries, is a tree.

clue.text: Around that place see ancient tribe assembled

indicators.note: around says the tribe's name surrounds the word for that place

parts.note: Gad was one of the twelve tribes of Israel
there means that place

explanation.surface: An old tribe is seen gathered around a particular spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is only a link word, and 'Around' tells the tribe to wrap round the place word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gathered means collected together, a synonym.

clue.text: Marketing chap is maniac who's lost his head

indicators.note: losing his head means the first letter of the word for maniac is dropped

parts.note: a maniac is a madman

explanation.surface: An advertising man is a crazy fellow who has gone off the rails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who's lost his head' takes the M off MADMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An advertising executive works in selling, so he is a marketing man.

clue.text: Like attractive figure presented by old-timer

definitions.meaning: an ... figure is a curvy, shapely one, so the word describes it
an old-fashioned timer using running sand

explanation.surface: A shapely figure is shown off by a veteran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old-timer' looks like a veteran, but it is literally an old device for timing.
explanation.definitionFit: The sand timer narrows at the waist, which is why a curvy body shape is named after it.

clue.text: Drink has sailor in a spin after dance

parts.note: rum is a drink

indicators.note: in a spin means the word for sailor is turned round

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: A drinking sailor's head is spinning after a night of dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the end, joined by 'after'; 'in a spin' turns only the sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cuban ballroom dance is a kind of dance.

clue.text: An exchange of punches and what ends it?

definitions.meaning: a heated fight or slugging match
the sound of the bell that ends a boxing round

explanation.surface: A boxing bout and what brings it to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy fight is informally a ding-dong, and the bell rung to stop a round makes that sound.

clue.text: Unsophisticated 'husband has some awful joke

indicators.note: awful signals that the letters of the word some are badly arranged

parts.note: a pun is a joke

explanation.surface: A simple husband tells a terrible joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' turns SOME into OMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Homely or plain things are unpolished, without refinement.

clue.text: Adequate space for joint exercise?

parts.note: literally, enough space for the arm joint to move; in fact the phrase means space to work freely

explanation.surface: Enough room for a group workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint exercise' reads as exercise done together, but the joint is the arm's.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means enough space to move freely, from room to move one's arms.

clue.text: Discourage fellow on international mission, maybe

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the fellow piece follows the international piece

parts.note: UN, the United Nations, runs international missions
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A man on a peacekeeping mission loses heart.
explanation.definitionFit: To unman is to deprive of courage, to dishearten.

clue.text: Gaps woman found in fabric full of holes

indicators.note: found in says the woman sits within the fabric

parts.note: lace is an open-work fabric full of holes
Una is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Some gaps were spotted by a woman in a holey material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabric full of holes' is a playful description of an open-work material rather than a plain synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacunae are blanks or missing parts, the plural of lacuna.

clue.text: Stingy person endlessly pulling back

indicators.note: back tells us the shortened word is read in reverse
endlessly means the last letter of the word for pulling is removed

parts.note: dragging means pulling

explanation.surface: A miser keeps drawing back without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims DRAGGING to DRAGGIN, and 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A niggard is a miser, someone mean with money.

clue.text: Signs of the times may be seen in such activity

definitions.text: Signs of the times may be seen in such activity

parts.words: Signs of the times may be seen in such activity
parts.note: the times sign is the cross used in arithmetic, seen when working out products

explanation.surface: Indications of the age are visible in certain events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Signs of the times' suggests trends of the age, but means the × symbols of arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Working out products uses the times sign, so this arithmetic is where it appears.

clue.text: Criticise what a monopolist's unwilling to do

definitions.meaning: to tear apart or pull to pieces in criticism

definitions.text: what a monopolist's unwilling to do
definitions.meaning: a monopolist wants the whole, not a share

explanation.surface: Attacking what a monopoly holder refuses to do.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull to pieces verbally is to slate or criticise.

clue.text: Exercising power at place of work

definitions.meaning: literally at the workplace, in the office

explanation.surface: Wielding authority at the workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A government holding power is said to be in office, and a worker at a desk is literally there.

clue.text: Rising. fragrance ain't bad around lover

indicators.note: around says the jumbled letters enclose the fragrance word
bad signals that the letters of ain't are muddled
in a down clue rising means the fragrance word is read upwards

parts.note: an aroma is a fragrance

explanation.surface: A scent that is not unpleasant surrounds a sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: The full stop after 'Rising' is a print slip; 'bad' gives INTA, which 'around' wraps round AMORA.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a female beloved, a sweetheart.

clue.text: Place of dubious existence ÷in short, not one to be found in book of maps

indicators.note: to be found in puts the shortened word and one inside the book of maps

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps

indicators.note: in short means the following word is abbreviated, losing its middle letter

parts.note: NOT shortened, as in the contraction n't
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A mythical place, not listed in any atlas.
explanation.walkthrough: The ÷ is a print slip for a dash; 'in short' abbreviates 'not' as in the contraction n't.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary sunken island may never have existed, so it is a mythical place.

clue.text: Lear's potentate could be what? Do ask — often

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters of the following words can be rearranged into the answer

explanation.surface: A puzzled reader asks repeatedly who the ruler in Lear's poem is.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear wrote a nonsense poem about this ruler, which keeps asking 'Who, or why, or which, or what'.
explanation.definitionFit: The title figure of an Edward Lear nonsense poem is a ruler, a potentate.

clue.text: Excessively formal and not very interesting to have for dinner

definitions.text: Excessively formal and not very interesting

explanation.surface: Dull and pompous, and something one might eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is heavy food, and a dull, staid person is called that too.

clue.text: Territory controlled by Montgomery

parts.note: suggests the British field marshal's command, but Montgomery is a city that is a US state capital

explanation.surface: Ground held by Field Marshal Montgomery.
explanation.walkthrough: Montgomery suggests the British WWII general, but the city of Montgomery is the state capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Montgomery is the capital of this US state, the seat of its government.

clue.text: Orphan protected by grannies

indicators.note: protected by means the answer is held within the following word

explanation.surface: A parentless child is looked after by grandmothers.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Orphan Annie is the famous orphan of the comic strip and musical.

clue.text: Stroll accomplished, maiden goes inside

indicators.note: goes inside says the maiden letter is placed within the word for accomplished

parts.note: able means skilled, accomplished
M is a maiden over in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A skilled young woman goes inside for a gentle walk.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, written M.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a leisurely pace.

clue.text: Happen to disagree

definitions.meaning: to turn out, as in 'as it fell out'

explanation.surface: Arguments do happen.
explanation.definitionFit: Events that come about are said to fall out, and friends who quarrel do too.

clue.text: Sign made by one supporter after end of trial

indicators.note: after says the one and supporter pieces follow the end letter
end of picks the final letter of the word trial

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a bra supports

explanation.surface: A signal given by a backer once a trial has finished.
explanation.definitionFit: The scales are one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Old garment with new cut in Pacific islands

indicators.note: cut in means the new letter is inserted into the garment

parts.note: a toga was a Roman garment

explanation.surface: An old robe is altered with a fresh cut, in the South Seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut in' puts N inside TOGA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is an island kingdom in the South Pacific.

clue.text: It ensures proper sitting to support the directors

parts.note: to back is to support
a company's board is its directors

explanation.surface: A good posture policy supports the company's executives.
explanation.walkthrough: A board placed behind the back keeps one sitting upright.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigid board behind the back helps someone sit upright with good posture.

clue.text: Peat's scattered around small flowering plant

indicators.note: around says the jumbled letters surround the word for small
scattered signals that the letters of peat's are strewn into a new order

parts.note: wee is Scots for small

explanation.surface: Peat has been spread round a little bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' looks like part of the definition 'small flowering plant', but it supplies the Scots word inside the jumble STPEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing garden annual with fragrant blossoms is a flowering plant.

clue.text: High-level secretary needed in lively ecclesiastical office

indicators.note: needed in says the secretary goes inside the word for lively

parts.note: pacy means fast, lively
a PA is a personal assistant, a senior secretary

explanation.surface: A senior secretary is wanted in a busy church office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-level' tells us the secretary is a personal assistant to someone senior.
explanation.definitionFit: The papacy is the office of the Pope in the Church.
